Who Told You You Couldn't Sing?

What if “I can't sing” isn't actually a fact about your voice — but a story you've been carrying for years?

This short guided experience will help you uncover where that story came from, question whether it still belongs to you, and take one small, practical step towards discovering what your voice might actually be capable of.

Start with curiosity.

By signing up, you'll receive the audit and a short follow-up series from Julie. You can unsubscribe at any time.
Before technique comes story

You may have decided something about your voice a very long time ago.

Perhaps a teacher told you to mime. Perhaps someone laughed. Perhaps you simply stopped singing and somewhere along the way decided that singers were other people.

“I can't sing” can sound like a fact. Very often, it is simply the conclusion we reached before we ever had the chance to learn.

I'm Julie Bale, a dramatic soprano, Vocal Transformation Specialist and Mentor. I've spent more than 35 years working with voices. What fascinates me is not only how a voice develops technically, but what happens when an adult begins to question the story they have been carrying about it.

5 of 8 · Your tiny experiment

Sing for 60 seconds.

Choose a song you know very well. Stand comfortably. Take an easy breath. Sing the first verse.

One rule: you are not allowed to decide whether it was “good”.

Instead, notice:

BackI've tried it
6 of 8 · Reframe

What if the question isn't “Can I sing?”

What if the better question is:

“What could my voice become if I learnt how to use it?”

Adults can develop coordination, listening, breath, musical confidence and performance skill later in life. You are not trying to become the singer you might have been at 20. You are discovering the singer you can be now.

BackContinue
7 of 8 · One honest question

If you knew you would be supported rather than judged, would you like to discover what your voice could actually do?

BackSee my final thought
8 of 8 · Your new starting point

Perhaps the problem was never that you couldn't sing.

Perhaps you simply never had the right opportunity to discover your voice.

You do not need to decide today whether you are a singer. You do not need to know whether you are “good enough”. Curiosity is enough.

If that curiosity has been stirred, the next step is simply to explore what happens when your voice is given proper attention, guidance and somewhere safe to grow.
